functions.sdk_source: Not part of libultra. The routine is Nintendo's Yay0 decoder as also shipped hand-written in Paper Mario (pmret/papermario src/os/decode_yay0.s, under that decomp's os/ directory). It is a Nintendo-provided assembly routine reused across titles; no original SDK file name is asserted.
evidence: Trapping (signed-overflow) arithmetic, 16 instructions (3 add, 12 addi, 1 sub): add at 0x800D8E70 `add t8,t8,a1` (0305C020), 0x800D8E74 `add a3,a3,a0` (00E43820) and 0x800D8E78 `add t9,t9,a0` (0324C820); addi at 0x800D8E7C `addi a0,a0,0x10` (20840010), 0x800D8E90 (20840004), 0x800D8EA4 (23390001), 0x800D8EB0 (20A50001), 0x800D8EB8 (20E70002), 0x800D8ECC (216B0002), 0x800D8ED4 (216BFFFF), 0x800D8ED8 (21290001), 0x800D8EE4 (20A50001), 0x800D8EF0 (20C6FFFF), 0x800D8F00 (23390001) and 0x800D8F08 (216B0012); sub at 0x800D8EC8 `sub t1,a1,t2` (00AA4822). Rabbitizer decode of ROM 0xABEA0..0xABF4F: scratch/omp/wave15/o2/r2work/decode-800D8E60.txt (command: uv run --frozen python scratch/omp/wave15/o2/r2work/decode.py d8e60), final count line {'add': 3, 'addi': 12, 'sub': 1} 16. match.py's disassembly flags each one as a handwritten instruction.
Sign test on the code word: 0x800D8E94 `slt t1,t0,zero` then 0x800D8E98 `beqz t1`. Both compilers branch on a sign with bltz/bgez, not slt plus beqz on a zero register.

Unconditional branches use `b` (beq zero,zero) at 0x800D8EAC and 0x800D8F04. The decrement of the bit counter is hand-placed in the loop-closing delay slot at 0x800D8EF0 (`addi a2,a2,-1`). This is .set noreorder hand scheduling.

The instruction words are identical to Paper Mario's hand-written decoder: all 43 words of 0x800D8E60..0x800D8F08 equal pmret/papermario src/os/decode_yay0.s (0x8006EDF0..0x8006EE98), and both end with the same padding nop. Branch offsets are PC-relative, so the bytes compare directly. Reference copy: scratch/omp/wave15/o2/sdk_ref/papermario_src_os_decode_yay0.s.
